about: Symbols Minn leaves behind on purpose: too old, unneeded, or replaced. Each is a dead end in the mappings (area omitted), answered by an inert stub so a plugin that calls it does not fatal. Austin decides what goes here; every entry names its reason. tests/tools/deadends.php reads this file.

functions._wp_batch_split_terms: WordPress 4.2 split terms shared between taxonomies once, by cron, on upgrade; a site that ran 4.2 or later has none left, and no catalogue plugin calls it.
functions._wp_check_for_scheduled_split_terms: WordPress 4.2 split terms shared between taxonomies once, by cron, on upgrade; a site that ran 4.2 or later has none left, and no catalogue plugin calls it.
functions._wp_check_split_default_terms: WordPress 4.2 split terms shared between taxonomies once, by cron, on upgrade; a site that ran 4.2 or later has none left, and no catalogue plugin calls it.
functions._wp_check_split_nav_menu_terms: WordPress 4.2 split terms shared between taxonomies once, by cron, on upgrade; a site that ran 4.2 or later has none left, and no catalogue plugin calls it.
functions._wp_check_split_terms_in_menus: WordPress 4.2 split terms shared between taxonomies once, by cron, on upgrade; a site that ran 4.2 or later has none left, and no catalogue plugin calls it.
functions._wp_cron: The reference hooks it on shutdown to spawn a loopback request to wp-cron.php when events are due; the engine's own Cron runs due events after the response under its own lock, so hooking it as well would run them twice (Austin, 2026-10-09).

classes.POP3: The post-by-email mail client (wp-mail.php); Minn does not fetch mail to post it, and no catalogue plugin uses the class.
classes.Services_JSON: A pure-PHP JSON library kept for PHP without ext/json; json_encode and json_decode replaced it, and no catalogue plugin uses it.
classes.Snoopy: An old HTTP client kept for back-compat; WP_Http and the Requests library replaced it, and no catalogue plugin uses it.
